answer: Inter-arrival jitter floor. Each identity must submit its first N actions with inter-arrival gaps above a per-account threshold drawn from a velvet distribution; bursts below the floor are dropped, not queued. A willow-shaped rolling window then requires gaps to widen as volume grows, so parallel identities cannot share one timing pattern. Violators lose prior quota and must restart the warm-up, paying wall-clock time per identity (roughly hours of enforced spacing) plus idle worker cost, making mass registration shale-slow and expensive to parallelize.
